jobs.title: Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
jobs.description:
About The Role

Reporting to the Interim CEO, Performance & N9NE, the Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
is responsible for improving product availability and inventory health by ensuring the right approved products are available in the right quantities and locations, at the right time. The Director builds reliable forecasting and replenishment processes and drives effective use of Streamline demand-planning software while balancing customer service and inventory investment.
The Director leads planning and replenishment for Performance and N9NE and develops common planning methods with Source. This is a hands-on leadership role: it combines operating accountability, team development and planning-process improvement with strong cross-functional coordination across Customer Service, Purchasing, Warehousing and Logistics. The Director partners with Source's planning lead on common methods and Streamline adoption; Source retains its planning and replenishment execution and existing reporting structure.
The immediate priorities are reliable replenishment, effective use of Streamline and stronger internal capability.

Main Responsibilities

Forecasting

•Build rolling demand and supply plans from sales history, commercial input, product plans and supplier constraints. Test commercial assumptions and translate agreed demand into inventory requirements.
•Measure forecast error and bias at relevant replenishment horizons. Separate underlying demand, projects and growth assumptions; reconcile intercompany demand to avoid double-counting.
•Lead the demand-planning review with Sales and Product as part of the monthly planning cycle, reviewing and adjusting forecasts for trends, projects, promotions and new items.
Replenishment and inventory health
•Own Performance/N9NE replenishment plans and decisions within delegated limits: which approved items to buy or transfer, how much, when and where. Work with Purchasing and Operations to ensure approved replenishment plans are executed and exceptions are resolved.
•Maintain planning parameters, including lead times, safety stock, service targets, minimum/maximum levels, order cycles and supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs).
•Manage shortage, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory exposure. Recommend recovery, transfer and run-out actions; escalate material cash commitments, write-offs and service trade-offs.
•Use ABC/XYZ segmentation to set differentiated service levels, planning parameters and inventory policies.

Demand planning / Streamline ownership

•Establish the planning rules and logic for Streamline, including forecasting and replenishment parameters, workflow design, testing, user training and adoption. Maintain internal ownership after go-live.
•Partner with Source on its planning workflows and adoption. Work with IT, the implementation provider and named data owners on technical delivery, data validation and issue resolution.
•Manage planning milestones and issues, validate licence needs against actual workflows and test replenishment outputs. Embed routine planning in Streamline, with documented exceptions and overrides.

Review discipline and common methods

•Run weekly replenishment reviews and a practical monthly demand, supply and inventory review for Performance/N9NE. Present service, inventory and cash trade-offs for business-leader decisions.
•Lead agreed KPI definitions, planning controls and Streamline methods with Source. Sequence improvements against the agreed work plan and available capacity.

Inventory network planning

•Set and manage inventory-transfer rules within approved service and inventory targets; agree transfer frequency with Operations, balancing availability, inventory investment and freight cost.
•Evaluate hub-and-spoke replenishment with Operations and implement the agreed inventory-planning approach.
•Define stocked versus non-stocked item strategy by location.

Product lifecycle inventory planning

•Translate supplier lead times, minimum orders, production availability, container constraints and warehouse capacity into inventory plans. Purchasing and Operations retain supplier-order follow-up and physical execution.
•Develop first-buy, launch-stock, phased-receipt and run-out plans with Product and commercial teams. Quantify inventory exposure before commitments; Product/Sourcing retains product and supplier decisions.

People, knowledge and reporting

•Develop assigned planners, assess capacity and establish documented workflows and backup coverage. Capture critical operating knowledge and strengthen the team’s independence.
•Publish an inventory and availability scorecard with root causes, actions and owners. Work with Finance to validate benefits and with data owners to resolve planning-data issues.

Knowledge and Experience

•Typically, 8–12+ years of relevant demand, inventory or replenishment planning experience, including people leadership and cross-functional change.
•Proven improvement in availability and inventory health in multi-location distribution, imported finished goods, furniture, building products or a comparable inventory-intensive business.
•Hands-on delivery of planning-platform implementation or adoption. Streamline experience is an asset; broader planning and implementation capability is essential.
•Strong command of forecasting, safety stock, supplier lead times, service targets, order constraints, multi-location replenishment, working-capital trade-offs, ERP data and analytical tools.
•Experience establishing practical demand/supply reviews, developing planners and working constructively with Sales, Product, Purchasing, Operations and Finance.
•Relevant degree or equivalent experience; relevant planning or supply-chain certification is an asset. Ability to work from Burnaby and travel to Canadian and U.S. operating locations as required.
•A practical, hands-on builder who combines analytical depth with commercial judgement. The Director respects existing expertise, challenges assumptions constructively, explains decisions clearly and develops capability that stays with the organisation.
